speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: Intersection homology, duality, and the L2 comparison
summary: The dated Fuchs heading begins on P000917; the first line of P000918 finishes the discussion of Deligne’s construction. The talk explains allowable chains, Poincar\'e duality, the two-sphere nodal example, a proposed comparison with \(L^2\)-cohomology, and isolated-singularity truncation. This continues the subject indexed in 1979-484.1--4. The catalogue’s P000916 is an undated continuation of Zakharov’s Benney-equation discussion already indexed as 1979-488.1--7: hydrostatic equations, height conservation, additional conservation laws, a Hamiltonian layer formulation, a two-horizontal-dimensional extension, kinetic interpretation, and Gelfand’s collective-equation remark. It is covered here by this explicit boundary cross-reference, without creating a second occurrence or attributing it to Fuchs.

speaker: M. I. Graev
title: Admissible families of curves and local integral geometry
summary: Graev’s actual heading is on P000918. He discusses weighted curve transforms, differential forms on curves through a point, the distinction between closure and point-supported inversion when that incidence fiber is one-dimensional, and quotienting trivial exact forms. The two explicit FA references are identified separately: Gelfand--Gindikin--Shapiro, 13(2), 1979, and Gelfand--Graev, 14(4), 1980; the second does not have the same author list. The preceding Fuchs and Zakharov material is not reassigned to Graev.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Double fibrations, differential equations, and Segre structures
summary: The actual talk occupies P000919--P000921. It passes from a two-parameter family of plane curves and its dual differential equation to incidence double fibrations, homogeneous examples, separate-coordinate equivalence, and the coframe definition of Segre structures. The explicit Inventiones reference is Faran’s 1980 paper. P000922 begins the separately dated 20 October session, so its Goncharov, Fuchs and Beilinson interventions belong to record 493. The second-order-equation discussion recurs from 1976-403.1--5.

speaker: A. B. Goncharov
title: G-structures, intersection complexes, and regular holonomic systems
summary: The session begins on P000922 with Goncharov’s definition of a G-structure and a problem about geometries on the sphere. Fuchs then revisits allowable chains, and Beilinson explains intersection complexes through differential operators, minimal extension and the regular Riemann--Hilbert correspondence, continuing through P000924. These interventions are expressly headed in the manuscript although absent from the short catalogue label. P000925 begins 27 October and belongs to records 494--495.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Elementary group problems and projective structures on the line
summary: The dated heading is on P000925. The problems concern finite symmetry groups, the topology and group law of the universal cover of SL(2,R), a triple-line cocycle, and Kirillov’s classification of locally projective structures on the real line. The material ends above Gaveau’s heading on P000926. The catalogue’s preceding P000924 still belongs to the 20 October D-module discussion.

speaker: Bernard Gaveau
title: Levi-flat fillings and gauge-covariant stochastic constructions
summary: Gaveau’s heading begins near the bottom of P000926 and continues through P000928. The first topic concerns envelopes of holomorphy and disc fillings of spheres in complex dimension two; the second constructs gauge-covariant diffusion on connection spaces with a fixed heat-kernel cutoff; the final formulas concern Feynman--Kac, spectral growth and exponential moment estimates. His brief list of possible topics is not evidence that a full scattering theorem was stated. P000929--P000930 begin the dated 3 November session and are not part of this talk.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Representation theory, noncommutative birational geometry, and sheaves
summary: The actual intervention occupies P000929, headed I.M.G. and History of representation theory. Its historical list runs through characters, Haar integration, operator algebras and Lorentz-group representations; these names are contextual remarks, not newly stated theorems or a reliable exclusive priority list. The mathematical content concerns enveloping algebras, the Gelfand--Kirillov birational conjecture, a poorly specified extension beyond polynomial coefficients, and the BGG sheaf method on projective space. The subsequent Beilinson heading on P000930 starts record 496. The Gelfand--Kirillov problem is the earlier GP-1967-21, not a new 1980 problem.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: D-affinity and localization on the flag variety
summary: The Beilinson heading is on P000930, following Gelfand’s separately catalogued historical introduction on P000929. His talk continues through P000932, outside this record’s short catalogue range. It moves from affine schemes and quasi-coherent sheaves to D-affinity, induced modules, left/right operator issues and the Beilinson--Bernstein localization theorem at the trivial infinitesimal character. The uncertainty about the converse categorical criterion is resolved in his 10 November continuation, record 498.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Cayley numbers, absolute-valued algebras, and projective planes
summary: The actual intervention is the upper part of P000933, before Beilinson’s heading. Its questions concern multiplicative norms, the finite-dimensional restriction, a possible infinite-dimensional example, projective-plane coordinatization and a geometric approach to exceptional Lie theory. The notebook does not state a unit axiom. That omission changes both the finite classification and the answer to the infinite-dimensional question, and is recorded explicitly. No content from Beilinson’s following pages is assigned to this record.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: A-affinity, projective generators, localization and transfer bimodules
summary: The actual heading is in the lower part of P000933; the talk continues through P000936. It proves the categorical affinity criterion left uncertain on 3 November, formulates the compact projective generator lemma, repeats projective-space and flag-variety localization, and begins the transfer-bimodule construction. The preceding Cayley-algebra intervention on the same page is record 499. The short catalogue range stops before most of the proof and must not determine the content boundary.
